text:
alex: heads-up — perf run on canary shows a ~12% host-side tail when grpc requests cross ~16KB. looks correlated with ragged chunk boundaries from the ingress framer and extra tokenization passes.

sam: can you attach the flame graph or top output? curious if it's syscall or CPU.

alex: pasting a trimmed perf snippet: 
```
  samples by function: 
  ingress_framer: 34%
  token_parse: 22%
  writev_coalesce: 10%
  kv_cache_lookup: 6% (mostly hits)
  kernel_selector: 5% (memcpy hot)
```

maria: interesting — kv cache hit rates are stable, but heatmap shows hot keys skewed to a few shards. That can cause micro-contention on the parser side because of lock handoffs.

ashley: also seeing more small write syscalls from http2 small-frame boundaries. HTTP/2 -> grpc shim is creating many 1-2KB fragments; each triggers tokenize+parse.

kai: could be kernel selection mismatch: we pick the short-seq kernel for smaller batches but some requests get misclassified after framing and we memcpy into contiguous buffer which kills throughput.

sam: is this a regression or long-standing?

alex: regression after the framing change two deploys ago — earlier builds coalesced bytes at a cheaper layer. canary diff + screenshots attached in the thread (cc @maria).

maria: quick mitigation ideas:
- bump ingress framer to coalesce up to 32KB before handing to parser (config flag)
- change kernel selector to use post-coalesce length estimate to avoid memcpy fallback
- add a small writev aggregator on host to reduce syscall count on http2 path

ashley: agree. the writev aggregator alone dropped syscalls by ~40% in my local microbench.

kai: for longer-term: update batching heuristics to prefer grouping ragged streams by destination and sequence profile, so kernels see uniform lengths. also add a telemetry label when we choose short-vs-long kernel.

sam: who wants the triage ticket? /assign @alex @maria

alex: I'll open the ticket with repro steps, flame, and canary diff. planning a quick canary config to coalesce at ingress and rerun.

dev-bot: created perf-triage/INGRESS-827 — https://redwood.perf/INGRESS-827 — linked canary logs and flamegraphs. :eyes:

alex: leaving a note — if the coalesce config helps we'll push an A/B to Dedicated for 24h and monitor tail p99 and token cost.

maria: ping me if you need an experimental kv shard pin to rule out lock contention.

ashley: +1, and add a metric for small-frame syscall rate. that'll make rollback decisions easier. :thumbsup:
